precepts.text: Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt; she sent out her boughs unto the sea.
precepts.point: His boughs, Israel, were delivered to death in the nether parts of the earth, and the nations shook at his fall.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Pharaoh is asked who he is like in his greatness, and the answer is the great cedar: “Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches.” The Lord speaks to the prophets by similitudes, saying one thing that means another, and here he compares the Egyptian kingdom to Adam's kingdom, Adam ruling, to give us more insight into what we read in Genesis. “The waters made him great”: the waters that came from the Father made Adam great, flowing from him through all his plants, all Adam's children. And “his boughs were multiplied.” What are the boughs that multiplied?

Asaph answers in Psalm 80, crying to the “Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock”: “Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it. Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land. The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars. She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river.”

Those boughs are Israel, the sons of God. All of this is talking about Israel: all of us that were drinking that water, and everybody was not getting that water like us. Isaiah says the same: “In that day shall the branch of the Lord be beautiful and glorious.” The branches of the Lord are Israel, those of us that escape the destruction and get the kingdom.

So the boughs multiplied on the great cedar are Adam's true children, Israel, and the same vine the Lord brought out of Egypt and planted is the vine that filled the land with its shadow in Adam's kingdom.

precepts.text: Under the goodly cedar shall dwell all fowl of every wing.
precepts.point: His boughs, Israel, were delivered to death in the nether parts of the earth, and the nations shook at his fall.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Ezekiel 31 says the great cedar was “of an high stature”, and “All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs.” The fowls of heaven are the angels: all the angels were under Adam when he was ruling, as it says, “let all the angels of God worship him.” Under his branches the beasts of the field brought forth their young, and the serpent was “more subtil than any beast of the field”: Satan was there, under Adam. And “under his shadow dwelt all great nations”, all the nations of the earth.

Ezekiel 17 shows the same cedar planted again: “I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent.” That is talking about Christ. “In the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing; in the shadow of the branches thereof shall they dwell.” That is the same as Ezekiel 31. He will plant it in the height of Israel, where it was before.

“And all the trees of the field shall know that I the Lord have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish.” He brought us down, and he raises us back up again. Ezra saw it too: on mount Sion, in the midst of a great people, “a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest.”

To understand the kingdom of Adam you have to understand the kingdom that is to come. It will be the same thing: us ruling with Christ in righteousness, with all the fowl dwelling under the goodly cedar, and nobody able to hurt us.

precepts.text: Through envy of the devil came death into the world.
precepts.point: His boughs, Israel, were delivered to death in the nether parts of the earth, and the nations shook at his fall.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
The great cedar was so fair that “all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.” The fir trees were not like his boughs, the chesnut trees not like his branches. His boughs and branches were his true children, his firstborn in the heavens, immortal and ruling with him. The other trees were the children Adam had on the earth before the fall, not created in his image, the multitude “born in vain.” They envied him, and they envied the twelve tribes that were with him.

Wisdom of Solomon shows who else envied him: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity. Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world.” The man God created was Adam. Adam was immortal and his sons were immortal; the children he had on the earth were created as men, sons of men, and were not immortal.

The devil also envied Adam. Satan went to war with Adam, and when he could not get him, he went through his woman to take him down: he jumped on his wife, played with her emotions and tricked her. Through the envy of Satan, that is how death came.

It will be the same in the future: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee.” When Christ returns and sets us back on this earth to rule, the nations will envy us, the same as back then, but they will not be able to do anything against us.

precepts.text: They are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth.
precepts.point: His boughs, Israel, were delivered to death in the nether parts of the earth, and the nations shook at his fall.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
The great cedar that was lifted up in his height was driven out “for his wickedness”, and the Lord gives the end of it: “To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height, neither shoot up their top among the thick boughs, neither their trees stand up in their height, all that drink water: for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit.”

We are all delivered unto death. All that drank the water, his boughs, his branches, Israel, now have to come down on the earth and die as men. Before that we had our spiritual body, our angelic body. They go down “in the midst of the children of men” because they were not regular men. That goes back to “I have said, Ye are gods”, and “ye shall die like men.”

Read on: “In the day when he went down to the grave I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed.” The day Adam was cast out, the waters his boughs and branches were drinking were restrained. No water was coming to Adam anymore. Those great waters are the same living waters of Revelation 22; they stopped when Adam fell. Lebanon mourned for him and all the trees of the field fainted for him: his children.

“I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell.” Hell there is the grave, the earth. When Adam fell, the Lord withdrew paradise, a spiritual realm connected to the earth, and it caused devastation, and millions died, as Ezra says, “as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.” That is where Cain found his wife: not everybody died.

And “all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon”, Adam's top leaders, “shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth.” We are comforted here by the scriptures, “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

precepts.text: The trees in the garden of God are men among whom a man may seek to hide.
precepts.point: The trees of the garden here are people. Adam and his wife tried to hide their sins among the other people that were in the garden with them.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him: the fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chesnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.” The trees in the garden of God are men, and a man may seek to hide among them.

That is what Adam and his wife did. The trees of the garden here are people, and when they “hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God amongst the trees of the garden”, they were trying to hide their sins among the other people that were in the garden with them.

points: The great cedar, compared to Pharaoh, is read as Adam's kingdom.
The waters made him great, his boughs were multiplied, and all fowls nested in his branches.
The other trees of the garden envied him, and he was driven out for his wickedness.
His boughs, Israel, were delivered to death in the nether parts of the earth, and the nations shook at his fall.
